19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58

60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86

89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源

210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	---
214	
215	## 七、投稿前通用准备
216	
217	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
218	
219	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
220	- **不要用**：
221	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
222	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
223	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
224	- 风险：
225	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
226	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
227	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
228	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）

230	
231	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
232	
233	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
234	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
235	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
236	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
237	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
238	
239	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
240	
241	提交前必须逐一检查：
242	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
243	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态

245	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）

247	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
248	7. 所有专有名词有定义
249	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
250	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
251	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:exp-setup}
6	
7	We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across seven models from four base architectures (instruction-tuned, reasoning-specialized, and distilled variants) on four reasoning domains, with more than 2,400 total evaluation instances.
8	
9	\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B~\citep{guo2025deepseekr1}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq}. Parameter counts range from 7B to 32B.
10	
11	\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n=204$) provides formal logic problems with gold FOL annotations for the oracle control (\S\ref{sec:oracle}). ProofWriter~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} tests multi-step deductive reasoning ($n=600$). LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} evaluates logical reasoning ($n=200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} covers commonsense reasoning ($n=200$ for LLaMA-3.1-8B; $n=60$ for Qwen2.5-14B). GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n=30$) and AIME 2024 ($n=22$) serve as operating-regime probes.
12	
13	\paragraph{Parameters.} $K=12$ traces at $T=0.7$. Extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}=0.3$ (Appendix~\ref{app:prompts}). Z3~\citep{demoura2008z3} timeout: 10 seconds.
14	
15	\paragraph{Metrics.} Accuracy (\%), $C_0$ (\S\ref{sec:c0}), and $\Delta = \text{SICA} - \text{SC}$ in percentage points (pp). McNemar exact test at $\alpha = 0.05$; 95\% bootstrap CIs (10{,}000 resamples) for $n \geq 200$.
16	
17	
18	\subsection{Main Results: A Regime-Dependent Effect}
19	\label{sec:main-results}
20	
21	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports results across all conditions sorted by SC accuracy. SICA effectiveness depends on the model's baseline accuracy regime.
22	
23	\begin{table*}[t]
24	\centering
25	\small
26	\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all conditions, sorted by SC accuracy. $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). $\dagger$: $n \leq 60$ (suggestive). $\ddagger$: $n = 30$ pilot. $^\star$: interim. $^a$McNemar exact test. $^b$ICL with gold FOL examples. \textbf{Bold}: $p < 0.05$.}
27	\label{tab:main_results}
28	\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
29	\toprule
30	Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p^a$ \\
31	\midrule
32	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Very-low-accuracy regime (SC $\leq$ 40\%) --- Type C}} \\
33	Mistral-7B & PW-D5$^\star$ & 303 & 38.28 & 33.61 & $-$4.67 & --- \\
34	\midrule
35	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Goldilocks zone ($\sim$50--55\% SC)}} \\
36	Qwen2.5-14B & StrategyQA$^\dagger$ & 60 & 53.33 & 56.67 & $+$3.33 & 0.50 \\
37	Mistral-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 54.41 & \textbf{59.31} & $\mathbf{+4.90}$ & \textbf{0.013} \\
38	\midrule
39	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{High-accuracy regime (SC $\geq$ 63\%) --- Type A}} \\
40	LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 63.24 & 60.78 & $-$2.45 & 0.267 \\
41	DeepSeek-R1-7B & FOLIO+PW$^\dagger$ & 60 & 71.67 & 68.33 & $-$3.33 & 0.480 \\
42	LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
43	Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 73.70 & 74.24 & $+$0.54 & n.s. \\
44	Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO+PW & 804 & 76.24 & 76.49 & $+$0.25 & n.s. \\
45	Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 203 & 77.34 & 76.85 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
46	Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 78.50 & 78.00 & $-$0.50 & 1.000 \\
47	Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 83.82 & 84.31 & $+$0.49 & 0.655 \\
48	\midrule
49	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Degenerate ($C_0 < 5\%$)}} \\
50	QwQ-32B & AIME$^\dagger$ & 22 & 72.70 & 72.70 & 0.00 & --- \\
51	Qwen2.5-14B & GSM8K$^\ddagger$ & 30 & 96.67 & 96.67 & 0.00 & --- \\
52	\midrule
53	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold FOL/DSL + Z3)}} \\
54	Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & \textbf{89.71} & $+$14.22 & $<$0.001 \\
55	Qwen2.5-14B & ProofWriter & 600 & 75.17 & \textbf{86.67} & $+$11.50 & $<$0.001 \\
56	\bottomrule
57	\end{tabular}
58	\end{table*}
59	
60	SICA effectiveness exhibits a Goldilocks zone with three distinct failure modes. In the narrow favorable band ($\sim$50--55\% SC), SICA provides significant gains. Mistral-7B on FOLIO achieves $\Delta = +4.90$\,pp ($p = 0.013$, $b = 12$, $c = 2$, $n = 204$): 12 problems flip from incorrect to correct while only 2 flip in the opposite direction. Qwen2.5-14B on StrategyQA shows a directionally consistent $+3.33$\,pp ($n = 60$, suggestive).
61	
62	\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%): confirmation bias.} Eight conditions (SC $\geq$ 63\%, combined $N > 2{,}000$) produce $|\Delta| \leq 3.33$\,pp, all nonsignificant. Qwen2.5-14B across three powered datasets (FOLIO+PW $n = 804$, LogiQA $n = 200$) yields $|\Delta| \leq 0.50$\,pp. Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples (exp-044b: SC $= 73.70\%$, $\Delta = +0.54$\,pp, $n = 199$) fails to break the trap: improving extraction quality through exemplars does not overcome confirmation bias when the model already produces consistent traces. Qwen3-14B (SC $= 83.82\%$) shows generational improvement yet produces $\Delta = +0.49$\,pp ($p = 0.655$).
63	
64	\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%): noisy constraints.} When model accuracy is very low, traces are predominantly incorrect, and self-extracted constraints become noise. Mistral-7B on ProofWriter depth-5 problems (SC $= 38.28\%$, $n = 303$, interim) shows $\Delta = -4.67$\,pp: SICA \emph{actively hurts} performance. Constraints extracted from wrong traces encode incorrect reasoning as formal rules, and the solver amplifies rather than corrects these errors.
65	
66	The Goldilocks zone is narrow. The upper boundary is sharp: LLaMA-3.1-8B on FOLIO (SC $= 63.24\%$) already shows $\Delta = -2.45$\,pp. The lower boundary is equally clear: below $\sim$40\% SC, constraints transition from noisy-but-harmless to actively harmful. Two degenerate conditions (QwQ-32B, GSM8K) have $C_0 < 5\%$, reducing SICA to SC by construction. Figure~\ref{fig:regime_scatter} visualizes this regime dependence. \S\ref{sec:entropy} provides mechanism evidence. The oracle rows confirm that gold constraints yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter (both $p < 0.001$), proving the aggregation mechanism is sound when constraints are discriminative (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).
67	
68	\begin{figure*}[t]
69	\centering
70	\includegraphics[width=0.75\textwidth]{f2_regime_scatter.pdf}
71	\caption{SICA effectiveness by Self-Consistency accuracy. Solid markers: $n \geq 100$; hollow: $n < 100$. The Goldilocks zone (SC $\sim$50--55\%, green) yields the only significant gain ($+4.90$\,pp). Type A trap (SC $\geq$ 63\%, red): all conditions nonsignificant. Type C failure (SC $\leq$ 40\%, not shown in current figure): SICA actively hurts ($-4.67$\,pp, PW-D5 interim).}
72	\label{fig:regime_scatter}
73	\end{figure*}
74	
75	\subsection{Oracle Control: The Aggregation Mechanism Is Sound}
76	\label{sec:oracle}
77	
78	Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL formulas from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and DSL logic programs from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). The oracle evaluates each gold constraint against each candidate answer via Z3 directly, isolating constraint quality from aggregation mechanics.
79	
80	Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO versus 75.49\% for SC ($+14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$, $b = 29$, $c = 0$), with Z3 gold agreement of 95.1\% (194/204). On ProofWriter, Oracle-SICA reaches 86.67\% versus 75.17\% ($+11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$), with Z3 gold agreement of 97.1\% (577/594). Relational subtypes benefit most: RelNeg $+17.86$\,pp, RelNoneg $+13.01$\,pp (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:pw_oracle_subtype}).
81	
82	The oracle gaps define recoverable potential. Even Mistral-7B's significant $+4.90$\,pp captures only 34.5\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling ($+14.22$\,pp). Extraction quality remains the binding bottleneck across regimes.
83	
84	
85	\subsection{Entropy-Conditioned Analysis}
86	\label{sec:entropy}
87	
88	The regime boundary in \S\ref{sec:main-results} could reflect model architecture rather than accuracy. We condition SICA effectiveness on per-problem answer entropy for two models with contrasting aggregate outcomes on FOLIO-204: Mistral-7B ($\Delta = +4.90$\,pp) and Qwen2.5-14B ($\Delta = -0.49$\,pp on the same benchmark).
89	
90	\begin{table}[t]
91	\centering
92	\small
93	\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) by answer entropy. The aggregate regime difference is driven by the proportion of high-entropy problems in each model's distribution. Qwen2.5-14B high-entropy bin ($n = 21$) reflects $\approx$1 problem difference.}
94	\label{tab:entropy}
95	\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrr@{}}
96	\toprule
97	& \multicolumn{2}{c}{Mistral-7B} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Qwen2.5-14B} \\
98	\cmidrule(lr){2-3} \cmidrule(lr){4-5}
99	Entropy & $n$ (\%) & $\Delta$ & $n$ (\%) & $\Delta$ \\
100	\midrule
101	Low $[0, 0.5)$ & 65 (31.9) & 0.0 & 135 (66.2) & 0.0 \\
102	Med $[0.5, 1.0)$ & 66 (32.4) & $+$4.5 & 48 (23.5) & $-$4.2 \\
103	High $[1.0, \infty)$ & 73 (35.8) & $+$9.6 & 21 (10.3) & $+$4.8 \\
104	\bottomrule
105	\end{tabular}
106	\end{table}
107	
108	Table~\ref{tab:entropy} and Figure~\ref{fig:entropy_delta} show that answer entropy mediates SICA effectiveness. For Mistral-7B, gains increase monotonically with entropy: $+9.6$\,pp on high-entropy problems ($n = 73$, approximately 7 problems flipped). The aggregate $+4.90$\,pp is driven by this subpopulation, which comprises 35.8\% of Mistral's distribution vs.\ only 10.3\% of Qwen's.\footnote{Qwen2.5-14B's high-entropy bin ($n = 21$, $+4.8$\,pp) is directionally consistent but reflects approximately one problem difference; the medium-entropy reversal ($-4.2$\,pp) further suggests bin-boundary sensitivity. Finer-grained analysis is warranted when additional high-entropy data becomes available.} Qwen concentrates 66.2\% of problems in the low-entropy bin where SICA has zero effect. Stronger models produce more consistent traces with lower entropy, which limits the subpopulation where constraints can provide value.
109	
110	\begin{figure*}[t]
111	\centering
112	\includegraphics[width=0.75\textwidth]{f3_entropy_delta.pdf}
113	\caption{(a) Mean SICA $\Delta$ (pp) by answer entropy bin with 95\% bootstrap CIs. Mistral-7B gains increase monotonically with entropy; Qwen2.5-14B shows no reliable pattern (high-entropy bin $n = 21$, approximately one problem difference). (b) Entropy distribution: Mistral-7B allocates 36\% of problems to the high-entropy bin where SICA is most effective, vs.\ only 10\% for Qwen2.5-14B.}
114	\label{fig:entropy_delta}
115	\end{figure*}
116	
117	Mechanism metrics confirm the causal chain. Unanimous answer rate: 18.6\% (Mistral) vs.\ 58.8\% (Qwen). When SICA overrides SC, the override is correct 70.6\% of the time for Mistral but only 28.6\% for Qwen. Confirmation bias (fraction of problems where $>$80\% of constraints agree with the majority answer): 31.9\% (Mistral) vs.\ 62.3\% (Qwen). MAX-SAT satisfiability ratio: 0.961 (Mistral) vs.\ 0.991 (Qwen), evidence that Mistral's constraints contain more genuine tension for the solver to exploit. These metrics trace a causal path: high model accuracy $\rightarrow$ consistent traces $\rightarrow$ low entropy $\rightarrow$ high confirmation bias $\rightarrow$ non-discriminative constraints $\rightarrow$ MAX-SAT degenerates to counting.
118	
119	
120	\subsection{Constraint Ablation}
121	\label{sec:ablation}
122	
123	If high-accuracy constraints are non-discriminative, MAX-SAT should produce the same predictions as simpler rules. On Qwen2.5-14B (FOLIO + ProofWriter, $n = 804$), MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 803 of 804 predictions; wins (16) and losses (14) approximately cancel for a net gain of $+$2 problems (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:ablation}). Self-extracted constraints carry no signal beyond vote counts in the high-accuracy regime.
124	
125	
126	\subsection{Remediation Strategies}
127	\label{sec:interventions}
128	
129	Six strategies target distinct hypothesized causes of the capability trap across prompt, architecture, and solver dimensions (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:remediation}). None produces significant improvement. Contrastive prompting worsens discriminativeness (6.0\% vs.\ 8.2\% baseline). Cross-model extraction (Mistral-7B from Qwen2.5-14B traces) produces 0\% discriminative rate: trace structure determines constraint content regardless of extractor identity. Qwen3-14B lifts SC and SICA equally ($\Delta = +0.49$\,pp, $p = 0.655$). Solver-level interventions encounter structural barriers in each case: 0.9\% UNSAT trigger rate for Z3 feedback~\citep{kambhampati2024position}, reversion to SC at consistency filtering threshold $T \geq 4$, and 56.4\% of constraint pairs sharing zero Z3 variables across traces.

The Goldilocks result rests on Mistral-7B FOLIO performance, so we replicate with three random seeds to assess stability. All three runs use identical hyperparameters ($K = 12$, $T = 0.7$, $T_{\text{ext}} = 0.3$) on the full FOLIO evaluation set ($n = 204$).

\label{sec:failure-modes}

The regime-dependent pattern in Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reflects three distinct failure modes of self-extracted symbolic constraints.

\paragraph{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ $\sim$60\%).} Strong models produce consistent reasoning traces, and constraints extracted from those traces mirror the answer distribution. When most constraints support the same candidate, MAX-SAT excludes few clauses ($|\mathcal{C}^{\setminus}| \approx 0$), the penalty term in Eq.~\ref{eq:score} vanishes, and the scoring function degenerates to weighted vote counting (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). The ablation in \S\ref{sec:ablation} confirms this empirically: on Qwen2.5-14B (FOLIO + ProofWriter, $n = 804$), MAX-SAT and count-only baselines agree on 803 of 804 predictions.

\paragraph{Type B: non-formalizable domains.} LogiQA problems require pragmatic and contextual reasoning that resists clean FOL formalization. Mistral-7B on LogiQA achieves an extraction rate of 86.4\% (fraction of traces yielding at least one parseable constraint), but the resulting constraints have a contradiction rate of only 0.8\%. The condition sits in the Goldilocks SC range (51.00\%) yet produces $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), confirming that the right accuracy regime is necessary but not sufficient for SICA to help.

\paragraph{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ $\sim$40\%).} When model accuracy is low, the majority of traces reach incorrect answers. Constraints extracted from wrong traces encode incorrect reasoning as formal rules. Z3 treats these rules as soft clauses with weight proportional to their frequency, so the solver preferentially satisfies the wrong constraints and penalizes traces that happen to reach the correct answer. Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.0095$) demonstrates this effect: SICA converts a weak positive signal in trace diversity into a net negative by formalizing the errors.
